title: Mapping a function over a list does not change its length
statement: Applying a function to every element of a list (List.map) never changes how many elements the list has.

formal.statement: ((x0 : Sort (1)) -> ((x1 : Sort (1)) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : x0) -> x1)) -> ((x3 : List.{0} x0) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (List.length x1 (List.map x0 x1 x2 x3)) (List.length x0 x3)))))

evidence.supports: List.length_map is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example list_theorem_inventory -- List.length_map 2>/dev/null | grep -Fc '((x0 : Sort (1)) -> ((x1 : Sort (1)) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : x0) -> x1)) -> ((x3 : List.{0} x0) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (List.length x1 (List.map x0 x1 x2 x3)) (List.length x0 x3)))))')" -ge 1
